To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
combining annual blood pressure measurements over a few years in childhood improves the prediction of young adult values.

the correlation of blood pressure between childhood and young adulthood is increased when the average blood pressure over multiple years is used rather than a single year, and that the predictive value of blood pressure in childhood for young adult blood pressure is improved by using the average of blood pressure over multiple childhood years.
the correlations of BP measured in childhood with levels in young adulthood are increased by averaging BP measurements over several years in each childhood year.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for the prediction of blood pressure in young adults based on the combination of annual BP measurements in childhood.
the development of predictive models for blood pressure in young adults from childhood blood pressure measurements.
understanding the factors that influence the development of high blood pressure (BP), a major risk factor for heart attacks and strokes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
combining BP measurements over several years during childhood improves the prediction of young adult values, and that this improvement is due to the increase in tracking correlations.
the average of BP over several years in children increases the tracking correlation of BP between childhood and adulthood and improves the prediction for adult levels from childhood levels.
the average BP of a child is more important than a BP reading on a particular day.
The main takeaway from our work is that
combining BP data from several years in childhood can improve prediction of adult values.
combining multiple BP measurements over time in childhood can improve prediction of BP in young adult years.

the more often blood pressure is measured in childhood, the greater is the tracking of blood pressure into adulthood, and this is true even after controlling for the variability in blood pressure measurements over time.
